behavior_class_name: Backdoor Persistence Service Foothold Behavior Class
description: Creates persistence by registering a scheduled task using the Windows Task Scheduler 2.0 COM API. The task is configured with a logon trigger and executes under the SYSTEM account. Upon user logon, the Task Scheduler launches a benign marker application that writes a controlled artifact confirming persistence execution.

persistence_installer.role: initializes COM, connects to the Task Scheduler service, creates a logon-triggered scheduled task, and registers it to execute a marker payload under the SYSTEM account

marker_payload.role: benign executable launched by the scheduled task that continuously logs execution to confirm persistence behavior

registry: scheduled task registration stored under Task Scheduler subsystem
task configuration references SYSTEM execution context
process: Task Scheduler launches A06_3a_SampleApp.exe at user logon
marker process runs continuously after logon
file_system: log file contains repeated timestamped execution entries
host: Task visible in Task Scheduler GUI
Sysmon Event ID 1 may capture marker process execution
Task registration events may appear in Windows Event Logs (TaskScheduler/Operational)
network: no HTTP or HTTPS traffic is required
no TCP command channel is opened

code_placement: COM initialization, task creation, and registration logic are implemented in the installer executable. Persistent execution logging behavior is implemented in the separate marker payload executable.
execution_trigger: The installer executes manually. The persistence payload executes automatically when a user logs into the system via the Task Scheduler logon trigger.
execution_target: Scheduled Task subsystem and marker executable at C:\Users\Public\A06_3a_SampleApp.exe
semantic_meaning: Demonstrates scheduled task persistence using the Task Scheduler COM API, where a logon-triggered task executes a benign marker application under SYSTEM context to simulate real-world persistence mechanisms used by malware.

mitre_attack_mapping.note: Specifically aligns with Scheduled Task persistence via COM API and logon-triggered execution.

control_notes.payload_effect: writes a controlled log file confirming scheduled task persistence execution

success_conditions: installer successfully initializes COM and connects to Task Scheduler
existing task A06_3a_LogonTask is deleted if present
new scheduled task definition is created
task is registered under SYSTEM context
user logs off and logs back in
marker begins writing log entries immediately
log file contains repeated timestamped entries confirming execution
no network activity or secondary payload execution occurs
